articles.title: Trump Faces Reduced Influence as Republican Party Loses Control of Congress
articles.summary: Incoming Democratic leaders have pledged to scrutinize top officials in Trump's administration and potentially prosecute individuals who do not cooperate with inquiries.
articles.content: President Donald Trump has announced plans to stage a political comeback despite his party's dismal performance in last week's midterm elections. The Republican Party lost control of Congress following Tuesday's vote, leaving Trump with limited influence for the remainder of his term as president. This 'lame duck' period will now span two years, significantly reducing Trump's ability to shape policy and legislation. Incoming Democratic leaders have pledged to scrutinize top officials in Trump's administration, promising to hold them accountable through investigations. The party has also threatened to prosecute certain individuals if they do not cooperate with inquiries. Trump responded to the news by taking to social media, where he expressed his discontent with the election results and their impact on the stock market, which had reportedly experienced a downturn following the vote. The appointment of Stephen Miller as Trump's new chief of staff marks a significant shift in strategy for the former president. Miller is known for his hardline stance on immigration, which has been identified by analysts as one of the key factors contributing to the Republican party's poor performance at the polls. This development comes as Democrats threaten to use their newfound control of Congress to launch investigations into Trump's administration. The party has signaled its intention to summon officials, demand documents, and hold public hearings, putting Trump and his senior aides under intense scrutiny. Among the likely subjects for investigation are the Trump family's business dealings and cryptocurrency transactions, government contracts involving billionaire Elon Musk, cuts to federal agencies, immigration enforcement, and the conduct of the Iran war. These areas have already been identified as potential targets for Democratic probes. The Democrats' ability to summon officials and demand documents gives them significant leverage in their investigations. The party has control of committees in both chambers of Congress, allowing them to put pressure on Trump's administration from multiple angles. The impeachment threat against Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth has gained momentum within Republican ranks, with some lawmakers reportedly planning to introduce a motion as early as Monday. House Minority Leader Jeffries has signaled his support for an impeachment resolution, stating that Hegseth's leadership has been detrimental to national security and the economy. The criticism centers on Hegseth's handling of the conflict in Iran, which critics argue has led to increased costs for American consumers and compromised national safety. President Trump came to Hegseth's defense over the weekend, highlighting his successes in Venezuela and Iran as evidence of his effectiveness as Secretary of Defense. Trump pointed out that the US had successfully removed Venezuelan President Nicholas Maduro from power in January, resulting in significant financial gains for the country. Attorney General Todd Blanche has vowed to vigorously defend senior members of the administration, including White House advisor Stephen Miller, should they face prosecution or impeachment proceedings. The US Congress is continuing to clash over Democrat threats of prosecution against senior administration officials. Ranking Democrat Robert Garcia on the House Oversight Committee has fired back at Attorney General Todd Blanche's vow to defend White House advisors and cabinet members. Garcia has stated that it is the role of Congress to hold the executive branch accountable, insisting that Blanche's actions are driven by a desire to shield Donald Trump's administration from scrutiny. He has vowed to investigate those committing crimes against the public and stop corruption, undeterred by potential intimidation. articles.title: Seismic Activity Uncovered in Nankai Trough Region
articles.summary: Researchers at the University of Tokyo have employed a novel radiocarbon analysis technique to examine a sediment core extracted from the Kumano Sea off Japan's coast, uncovering multiple previously unknown earthquakes.
articles.content: Researchers at the University of Tokyo have employed a novel radiocarbon analysis technique to examine a sediment core extracted from the Kumano Sea off Japan's coast. The study has uncovered multiple previously unknown earthquakes in the Nankai Trough region, where a significant earthquake is forecasted to occur in the future. The Nankai Trough is an area known for its seismic activity and history of powerful earthquakes that have triggered devastating tsunamis. In recent years, Japan's disaster preparedness and monitoring systems have significantly improved, resulting in reduced damage from natural disasters compared to the past. A more accurate understanding of historical events, including their location, scale, and recurrence, is crucial for predicting future geophysical occurrences and mitigating potential disasters. The researchers' findings aim to contribute to this goal by shedding light on previously unknown seismic activity in the region. The study's results have been published in a scientific journal, but further research is necessary to confirm the significance of these hidden earthquakes and their impact on the region's seismic profile. A team of researchers from the University of Tokyo has employed a novel radiocarbon analysis technique to examine a sediment core extracted from the Kumano Sea. This effort aims to uncover signs of past earthquakes that conventional methods have been unable to detect. The study utilized an ultrasensitive method to measure the minute amounts of carbon-14 present in ocean floor sediments, with a resolution of 1 centimeter or less. This approach revealed several new geological layers not previously visible through visual observations or other analysis techniques. These newly discovered layers are thought to have originated from submarine landslides possibly triggered by earthquakes within the Nankai Trough region. The researchers' findings suggest that multiple events may have occurred in this area, which were not identified using conventional methods. The significance of carbon-14 lies in its predictable decay rate and widespread presence in biological materials. When organisms absorb carbon-14 during their lifetime, it can be measured in samples containing plant or animal remains. This allows researchers to date samples back approximately 50,000 to 60,000 years by tracking the extent of decay. The precise measurement of carbon-14 has enabled the team to uncover hidden geological events that would have otherwise gone undetected. A 40-centimeter-long cylinder of fine-grained clayey silt was extracted from the Kumano Trough, off Japan's southeast coast. This sediment core, obtained from a deep-sea trench, contains valuable information about past geological events that have affected the region. The researchers analyzed the total organic carbon content at regular intervals along the length of the core, measuring 0.5- to 1.0-centimeter segments. By doing so, they were able to pinpoint areas where older organic carbon was found mixed with younger sediment. This mixing is indicative of seafloor disturbance caused by severe floods, storms, or submarine earthquakes. The team's findings suggest that these events left behind hidden layers of sediment, which would have otherwise gone undetected. According to the researchers, "the chemical and structural features were indistinguishable" between redeposited sediments and the underlying material. This made it difficult to identify the affected areas without further analysis. By correlating their findings with historical records of submarine earthquakes from the 13th to the 20th century, the team was able to pinpoint specific events that had caused the seafloor disturbance. The precise measurement of carbon-14 has been instrumental in uncovering these hidden geological events, allowing researchers to gain a deeper understanding of the region's seismic history. Researchers are now looking to expand their analysis beyond the Kumano Sea, seeking a more comprehensive understanding of Japan's seismic history. This endeavor is crucial for regions prone to geological activity, as it can significantly improve predictive models and help mitigate disaster risks. By studying marine sediments in greater detail, scientists aim to uncover hidden patterns and events that have shaped Japan's geological landscape over time. articles.title: Apple Forced to Adopt Standard USB Ports on iPhones
articles.summary: MacOS fails to detect USB devices due to various reasons such as damaged cords or accessories requiring more power.
articles.content: USB devices have become an essential part of our daily lives, and Apple played a significant role in popularizing them with its iconic iMac design that ditched legacy connectors. The widespread adoption of USB ports led to European Union regulations forcing Apple to adopt standard USB ports on iPhones instead of its proprietary Lightning ports. Despite the prevalence of well-behaved modern USB Mac accessories, there are instances where macOS fails to detect them, causing frustration for users who expect seamless connectivity. This issue is not unique to specific devices or brands but can occur due to various reasons such as damaged cords or accessories that require more power. The good news is that many issues related to USB device detection on Macs have known explanations and fixes. For instance, if a cord is damaged, replacing it with a new one may resolve the problem. Similarly, some accessories might not work properly if they require more power than what's available from the Mac. In most cases, macOS software issues can be resolved by checking settings or permissions. By default, macOS requires user permission for accessories to connect, which prevents malware from being injected into the system. However, this also means that users may accidentally reject a permission prompt, preventing legitimate accessories from transmitting data until they give their consent. When a USB device is not detected on a Mac, it's essential to check if charging is still working in either direction. If charging works but the device is not recognized, it could be a sign of a software issue rather than a hardware problem. Forcing macOS to re-display permission prompts can resolve issues with unrecognized devices. To do this, try unplugging and replugging in the accessory. However, to avoid future hassle, it's a good idea to check your Mac's settings under Apple menu > System Settings > Privacy & Security. In the Accessories section of these settings, you'll find options for handling new accessories: Ask for new accessories, Automatically allow when unlocked, or Always allow. While Automatically allow when unlocked is a convenient option, it may not be suitable if you're frequently away from your Mac. If changing these settings doesn't resolve the issue, check to see if macOS recognizes your device in the first place. To do this, hold down the Option key and click on Apple menu > System Information. If your accessory appears under Hardware, you can refer to the manufacturer's online support resources for troubleshooting advice. However, if your accessory is not visible or is detected but results in an error message when plugged in, there may be a more complex issue at play. One possible cause of this problem is power: some devices require more power than a Mac's USB port can supply. In such cases, you might see related messages prompting you to connect a separate power cable. If your device doesn't have a separate power cord, the issue could lie with the USB port itself. Try using alternate ports on your Mac or connecting directly if you were previously using a hub or dock as an intermediary. If power-related warnings persist, it may be worth reaching out to Apple's technical support for assistance. This could indicate that there's an underlying problem with your Mac's ability to supply power through its USB ports. If your USB device isn't showing up on your MacBook, it's essential to consider the role that hubs and docks play in this process. These devices often require their own power supplies, but even if they don't, issues can arise when multiple devices are connected through a chain of transmission. One possible solution is to ensure that macOS is fully updated by navigating to System Settings via the Apple menu and clicking on Software Update. This could help resolve any bugs or driver compatibility issues that might be interfering with your USB device's functionality. Some accessories may rely on proprietary software, which requires regular updates to function correctly. To address this, check the Mac App Store for any available updates, or visit a manufacturer's website to download the latest version of their software. External storage devices such as cards and drives must use compatible file system formats, specifically APFS, FAT, or ExFAT, in order to be recognized by your MacBook. When troubleshooting USB issues, it's also crucial to verify that you're using the correct type of cable for a device's power and bandwidth requirements. Furthermore, inspect cables and ports for any signs of damage or debris, such as lint or bent pins, which can easily block functionality. Cleaning out lint and dust with an air can or soft-tipped tool may resolve issues related to debris, while replacing damaged cables is usually necessary if you notice browning or exposed wires, a clear indication of a potential fire hazard. articles.title: Joe Burrow Leads Bengals to Fourth Straight Win
articles.summary: Joe Burrow led his team to a 34-17 win over the Falcons, throwing four touchdowns and completing over 70% of his passes for the fourth straight game.
articles.content: The NFL season is heating up, and some players are standing out as top contenders for MVP. One way to measure a player's success is by their ability to perform under pressure, and Joe Burrow did just that in his team's 34-17 win over the Falcons. Burrow had an impressive game, throwing four touchdowns and completing over 70% of his passes. This marks the fourth straight game where he has achieved this feat, a first for any player in NFL history according to recent research. The Bengals' winning streak now stands at four games, with Burrow leading the charge. Ja'Marr Chase was instrumental in the team's victory, catching 10 passes for 155 yards and scoring one touchdown. Tee Higgins also had a notable performance, making five catches for 47 yards and two scores. These two players are widely regarded as one of the best wide receiver duos in the NFL. Chase's receiving skills were on full display, showcasing his ability to catch passes from anywhere on the field. He made eight catches in the first half alone, accumulating 142 yards and scoring a touchdown. This performance was just another example of Chase's exceptional talent as a wide receiver. The Bengals' win over the Falcons marked a significant moment for Burrow, solidifying his position as one of the top contenders for MVP. His impressive completion percentage and consistent passing skills have caught the attention of fans and analysts alike. Burrow's success on the field is not solely due to his talented teammates. Despite having a strong supporting cast, including Chase and Higgins, the Bengals' running game has been inconsistent, and their defense has struggled at times. Burrow's ability to perform under pressure and lead his team to victory in these situations makes him an attractive candidate for MVP. The Bengals' winning streak is a testament to Burrow's leadership and skills as a quarterback. With four straight games of exceptional performance, he is now firmly in the running for top honors. The MVP odds are currently favoring Joe Burrow, who is neck and neck with Josh Allen in terms of betting favorites. However, there's still a long way to go before the season concludes, and several factors could affect Burrow's chances. Weather conditions will likely change as the season progresses, which may impact Burrow's performance. Additionally, his history of health issues makes it essential to monitor his situation closely. Jordan Love is another strong contender for MVP honors, but his supporting cast leaves much to be desired. The Green Bay Packers' rushing attack is currently on pace for one of the worst marks in NFL history since the 1970 merger. Despite this, Love has been nothing short of spectacular, elevating Christian Watson and Matthew Golden to stardom alongside him. They recently became the first Green Bay wide receiver duo to both reach 150+ yards and score a touchdown in the same game. Love's impressive performances have also led to some remarkable statistics. He currently holds the top spot for completions 20+ yards downfield, with an astonishing 23 successful throws. The deep ball is undoubtedly one of Love's greatest strengths, showcasing his exceptional accuracy and ability to connect with his receivers over long distances. While Love is certainly a strong contender for MVP, he faces stiff competition from other talented quarterbacks. The team's offense was led by Puka Nacua, who received an astonishing 19 targets and responded with 14 catches for 150 yards and a touchdown. Matthew Stafford's performance was underwhelming, throwing an interception that seemed to come out of nowhere. This is not an isolated incident; he has thrown nine interceptions in as many games this season. His struggles on the field are becoming increasingly concerning, and it's unclear what adjustments can be made to improve his play. The Rams' quarterback situation has become increasingly concerning as the season progresses. His inability to connect with his receivers has become a recurring theme this season. This is a stark contrast to last year's numbers, where he had a 43% completion rate and an impressive 10-to-1 touchdown-to-interception ratio on such throws. articles.content: Canon has released its Dual Pixel 3D imaging software, a free tool designed to convert two-dimensional photographs into immersive three-dimensional images without requiring specialized equipment. The software's 3D converter app is available for download and allows users to generate photorealistic 3D models from their still images. However, it's essential to note that not all Canon cameras are compatible with this feature due to the system's reliance on Dual Pixel CMOS AF technology. Introduced by Canon in 2013, Dual Pixel CMOS AF is a sensor-based autofocus that features two photodiodes per pixel, enabling the camera to capture more detailed images. This technology is found in select iterations of the company's EOS R series cameras. The Dual Pixel 3D software utilizes this technology to convert phase differences into 3D renderings, making it possible to export images in OBJ, GLB, or MP4 video formats that showcase hyper-realistic depth and texture. This technology is a significant advancement in photography, allowing users to create stunning 3D models from their still images. However, the software's compatibility is limited to specific Canon cameras equipped with Dual Pixel CMOS AF technology. The EOS R series cameras that are compatible with this feature include several high-end models that were highly rated by critics in 2026. The availability of this software and its limitations will be explored further in subsequent parts of this article. Canon's Dual Pixel 3D imaging software has the potential to revolutionize the way photographers capture and display their images. However, users must ensure that their camera is compatible with this feature before attempting to use it. The compatibility issue may affect some users who own Canon cameras without the necessary technology. The free 3D photo software offered by Canon is available for download on their website, but users should be aware that the company's press release includes a caveat about potential changes to the specifications and terms of use in the future. To use the software, it is currently necessary to have the 2024 version or later of Windows 11 installed on your computer. The EOS R5 Mark II is one example of an EOS R camera that has received positive reviews from photographers due to its powerful specifications and capabilities. articles.title: US Tech Imports Pose Compatibility Risks
articles.summary: Buying technology from other countries can lead to issues with compatibility and functionality due to regional restrictions and varying hardware configurations.
articles.content: Buying technology from other countries may seem like a convenient solution when your device dies while traveling or when a product is not available locally. However, there are several drawbacks to consider before making an online purchase or buying in person during a trip. When importing devices, users often encounter restrictions that can be frustrating. For instance, the hardware configurations of certain products can vary depending on the region they were purchased in. Some devices may have features like dual SIM slots that are not available in other countries. For example, iPhones sold in China come equipped with physical SIM slots, a feature that was dropped from US models starting with the iPhone 14. This means users who purchase these phones abroad may struggle to access certain connectivity features when they return home. Additionally, some devices may have limited access to core software or tools even if they are used elsewhere. When shopping for technology from overseas markets, it's essential to research and understand any regional restrictions that may apply. This can help avoid unexpected problems with compatibility or functionality. Users who purchase devices from other regions may also face challenges in accessing warranty coverage or repair services, adding to the overall complexity of importing technology products. Purchasing technology products from other countries can be fraught with challenges, particularly when it comes to compatibility issues. One of the key concerns is cellular bands, which vary by region and country. For instance, a phone bought in another country may not work on the US' 5G network, resulting in limited access to carrier-specific features like VoLTE or Wi-Fi Calling. This can be a significant problem for individuals who plan to use their devices as main phones, making it essential to check the compatibility of any device before purchasing from outside one's home region. The issue is not limited to phones alone. Other tech products, such as laptops, can also pose problems when bought from abroad. For example, laptop keyboards may have different layouts depending on the country where they were purchased, with French keyboards featuring the AZERTY layout and QWERTY versions being less common in those markets. Moreover, power issues must be taken into account, including the need for adaptors due to differing plug types and voltages, which can range from 120V at 60Hz in the US to 220-240V at 50Hz in most of Europe and Asia. When shopping online from abroad, buyers must factor in additional costs such as import duties and shipping charges. The removal of the $800 de minimis exemption for international parcels by the US has increased the financial burden on consumers. With high shipping costs and potential tax liabilities, purchasing technology from overseas can be a costly affair. articles.title: Significant Discovery Made About Histone Role in Sperm Development
articles.summary: Researchers at Kyushu University have found that a specific histone subvariant, H3mm15, is crucial for regulating gene expression during spermatogenesis.
articles.content: Researchers at Kyushu University have made a significant discovery about the role of histones in sperm development. A team led by Professor Akihito Harada found that H3mm15, a specific type of histone H3.3 subvariant, plays a crucial part in regulating gene expression during spermatogenesis. Histones are protein molecules that act as spools around which DNA is wrapped, organizing the genome and controlling gene activity. H3.3 is a variant of histone H3 that is incorporated into chromatin independently of DNA replication and is associated with active genomic regions. The researchers had previously identified several closely related H3.3 subvariants in mice, including H3mm15, which differs from conventional H3.3 at just three amino acids. RNA analyses revealed that the gene encoding H3mm15 is predominantly expressed in the testis, raising questions about its distinct biological functions. A deeper investigation into the function of H3mm15 was conducted by Professor Harada's team, collaborating with researchers Qianmei Wu, Yasuyuki Ohkawa, and Tatsuya Takemoto. Their findings shed light on the importance of this specific histone subvariant in sperm development. The researchers' observations suggest that small differences in histone amino acid sequence can have significant effects on biological functions, a crucial insight into the regulation of gene expression during spermatogenesis. Mice lacking a specific histone protein variant called H3mm15 exhibited disorganized testis structures where sperm develop. Their sperm motility was also reduced and there were significant changes in gene expression related to spermatogenesis. The altered genes were particularly those involved in the transition from mitosis to meiosis, an essential step in sperm development. In cultured cells, H3mm15 was incorporated into chromatin less efficiently than another histone protein variant called H3.3, but showed a higher concentration near gene promoters where transcription begins. Analysis of transgenic mouse testes also revealed high levels of H3mm15-EGFP around the start sites of gene transcription. This suggests that H3mm15 plays an important role in regulating gene expression during spermatogenesis. The structural and biochemical properties of H3mm15-containing nucleosomes were found to be less stable than those containing H3.3, contributing to more dynamic chromatin association. The discovery of a distinct histone subvariant, H3mm15, has shed light on its role in regulating gene expression during spermatogenesis. The findings suggest that this specific histone variant plays a crucial part in establishing specialized chromatin environments necessary for normal sperm development. According to Harada, understanding the retention of closely related histone subvariants may provide insights into how cells create distinct chromatin properties through variations in genomic localization and stability dynamics. Further studies are needed before considering applications of H3mm15 to humans, but this research could ultimately help researchers interpret epigenetic abnormalities linked to impaired spermatogenesis. articles.content: Nvidia's board of directors has launched an investigation into the company's CEO, Jensen Huang, amid concerns over national security and potential ties to China. The probe comes after reports emerged that US officials suspect a Chinese intelligence asset had developed a close relationship with Huang. According to The New York Times, this individual, Alice Huang, was identified as a key figure in Nvidia's dealings with the Chinese government. Nvidia's CEO has already faced scrutiny over his personal life, with a memo circulated among employees revealing that he had been unfaithful to his wife. This revelation has sparked widespread discussion and debate within the tech industry. The implications of this investigation are far-reaching, given the sensitive nature of Nvidia's business dealings with countries like China, which have raised concerns about national security in the US. The investigation into Nvidia's business dealings has sparked a mix of reactions from experts and observers. Some have come out in support of CEO Jensen Huang, acknowledging his willingness to take responsibility for any mistakes made. This includes Bill Ackman, who praised Huang on social media, saying he is an "incredible human who makes mistakes like anyone else. However, not everyone shares this view. articles.content: The Gilded Age is a story that revolves around the intricacies of society and class, making family ties and marriages pivotal to its plot. To understand the complex relationships within this narrative, it's essential to unravel the web of connections between characters from prominent families such as the Scotts, van Rhijns, and Russells. At the heart of the story is Peggy Scott, a member of a prosperous Black family, who has an estranged relationship with her father, a pharmacist. Her decision to pursue a career in writing has put her at odds with him. Peggy's personal life is also marked by secrets: she had previously believed that her son Thomas was stillborn, but later discovers that he is alive and living with an adoptive family. Dorothy Scott's background as a pianist from Maryland played a significant role in shaping her life and relationships. It was during this time that she met her future husband, whose actions would have a lasting impact on their family. The couple's meeting took place in New York City when Peggy's father intervened to protect Dorothy from men who were following her. This chance encounter would eventually lead to the union of two families with distinct histories and social standing. Meanwhile, in Philadelphia, Thomas Spring was growing up three years old at the time, unaware that he had a biological mother who believed him to be stillborn. His life was marked by a different identity, one that his adoptive family had provided for him. As Peggy's respiratory illness worsened, her parents sought medical attention from Dr. William Kirkland, a physician with a personal connection to Arthur Scott. The doctor's family ties and background in medicine were influenced by his childhood acquaintance with Arthur Scott, who had later become a successful pharmacist in Brooklyn. Agnes van Rhijn's family ties are deeply rooted in the history of early New York City. Her husband Arnold was an investment banker from a wealthy family that had made their fortune in the city's early days. This influential background likely played a significant role in shaping Agnes's life and social standing. Ada Forte, Agnes's sister, is also a prominent figure in the story. She lives with Agnes and her children, including Oscar, whom she lovingly cares for as an aunt. Ada's relationship with Agnes is complex, however, and becomes increasingly strained when she meets Reverend Luke Forte and decides to marry him. The introduction of Reverend Luke Forte adds a new dynamic to the story. A devout Episcopal minister from Boston, he moves to New York City to assume a position at the Episcopal Church of Saint Thomas. His arrival sets off a chain of events that will have far-reaching consequences for the characters involved. Marian Brook, the niece of Ada and Agnes, is another key figure in this complex web of relationships. She comes from an estranged background with her aunts, but eventually finds herself living with them after being left without financial support following her father's passing. Her story becomes intertwined with that of Dashiell, a widower who is connected to the van Rhijn family through marriage and blood ties. Aurora Fane's family connections bring her into close proximity to Marian, a relationship that develops through their shared social status and familial ties. Oscar van Rhijn, Agnes' calculating son, is driven by a desire for wealth and social standing, which leads him to propose marriage to Gladys Russell. However, his interest wanes when he suspects the Russells may be facing financial difficulties. Unbeknownst to those around him, Oscar has a secret relationship with John Adams IV. Enid Turner Winterton van Rhijn's past as a maid for the Russell family is marked by scandal, as she was let go after attempting to seduce George Russell. Later in life, Enid marries Joshua Winterton and inherits his wealth and social standing upon his death, rising through the ranks of society. Bertha Russell's family fortune was built on the railroad industry, which made them extremely wealthy and enabled them to relocate to New York City. As a member of this new high-society circle, Bertha is determined to secure her family's place among Manhattan's elite. Her ambitions for her daughter Gladys are particularly strong; she wants her to marry someone with a respectable background. Bertha's husband, George, is a ruthless and cunning railroad magnate who has little time for union workers but shows great affection for his children, Larry and Gladys. Gladys's marriage to the Duke of Buckingham marked the beginning of a new chapter in her life. She left behind the excitement and glamour of New York to live with her husband in England. The Duke, despite his royal lineage, struggled financially, adding an air of uncertainty to their union. The union between Gladys and Hector produced a son, the Marquess of Sidmouth. Meanwhile, back in New York, Bertha's sister Monica attended Gladys's wedding, highlighting the complicated relationships within the family. During his visit to Buenos Aires, the pontiff was met with a mix of emotions, from enthusiasm to skepticism, as he navigated the complex landscape of Argentina's deep-seated divisions. articles.title: Perovskite semiconductor thin films developed with reduced defects
articles.summary: A team of researchers has made a breakthrough in developing high-performance perovskite semiconductor thin films with greatly reduced defects, paving the way for more efficient solar cells and LEDs.
articles.content: A team of researchers has made a breakthrough in developing high-performance perovskite semiconductor thin films with greatly reduced defects. The achievement is significant as it paves the way for more efficient solar cells and LEDs. The perovskite material platform offers low manufacturing costs and simple processing, making it an attractive option for next-generation electronic devices. This versatility has led to a surge in interest in using perovskites in both solar cells that convert light into electricity and LEDs that convert electricity into light. However, the formation of microscopic crystal grains during solidification often leads to defects at grain boundaries and surfaces. These imperfections can trap or eliminate photogenerated charge carriers, resulting in reduced device performance and operational lifetime. The team's innovative approach involves using a liquid-assisted crystal growth method to minimize these defects. By carefully controlling the solidification process, the researchers were able to create high-performance perovskite thin films with significantly fewer imperfections. The researchers turned their attention to a phenomenon known as eutectic melting, where combining certain materials can significantly lower their collective melting point. Specifically, they focused on the combination of methylammonium chloride (MACl) and zinc halide (ZnX₂), which have relatively high individual melting temperatures. When the perovskite film was gently heated to around 100°C, a liquid layer formed at the grain boundaries. This transformation enabled atoms to diffuse much faster than in a solid state, allowing small crystal grains to merge and grow into larger crystals with fewer defects. The presence of MACl facilitated rapid crystal growth, while zinc helped suppress defects by segregating towards the grain boundaries. As thermal annealing took place, MACl evaporated, leaving behind a cleaner crystal structure. As a result, the researchers obtained perovskite thin films with exceptional quality, rivaling those of passivated silicon in terms of performance. The charge-carrier lifetime reached approximately 295 μs and surface recombination velocity was reduced to 0.3 cm/s, marking significant improvements over previous reports for lead halide perovskites. The new crystal growth method has yielded significant improvements in the performance of perovskite solar cells and LEDs. Solar cells fabricated using these films have achieved a power conversion efficiency of 26.5%, along with an open-circuit voltage of 1.208 V. This certified record for solar cells with the same n-i-p architecture demonstrates the potential of this technology to revolutionize the field of renewable energy. The achievement of such high performance in both solar cells and LEDs suggests that a single device structure can function as either a power-generating or light-emitting device, opening up new possibilities for optoelectronic applications. According to Dr. Seongsik Nam, co-first author of the study, reducing surface recombination velocity is crucial for improving perovskite thin films. The new method has achieved a record-low surface recombination velocity of 0.3 cm/s, comparable to that of silicon. Professor Shin emphasized that the novelty of this research lies in its development of a crystal-growth method based on a volatile eutectic mixture, which fundamentally reduces defects in perovskites. This approach requires no expensive specialized equipment and is expected to find broad applications across various fields. The study on liquid-assisted crystal growth has shown promising results for reducing defects in perovskite materials used in solar cells and LEDs. This innovative approach involves using a volatile eutectic solvent to control the crystallization process of perovskites, allowing researchers to tailor the material's properties. The use of this technique is expected to have broad applications across various fields due to its simplicity and cost-effectiveness. The method has been successfully tested in laboratory settings, with promising results for efficient solar cells and LEDs. With further research and development, it may soon be possible to harness the full potential of perovskite materials in a wide range of optoelectronic devices. Liquid-assisted crystal growth is poised to make a significant impact on the field of perovskite optoelectronics, offering new avenues for researchers and industry experts alike. articles.title: Starlink Offers Resiliency Over Speed for Remote Areas
articles.summary: Satellite internet provides reliable connectivity in areas with limited landline infrastructure.
articles.content: A unique advantage of satellite internet has been identified that sets it apart from traditional providers. This perk is particularly relevant for individuals living in remote areas where access to landline internet services may be scarce or unreliable. In countries like the US, UK, and Canada, many communities have at least some basic landline option available, making it less likely for residents to choose satellite internet as a primary means of connectivity. However, there are certain situations where this type of service can prove to be invaluable. For instance, individuals who value resiliency over raw speed may find that satellite internet is the better choice. This adaptability is inherent in Starlink's design and could potentially save users from difficulties that arise when traditional internet services fail. The ability to access the internet virtually anywhere in the world is a significant benefit of satellite internet. When choosing the right plan, such as one of the various $55 options available, consumers can expect reliable connectivity even in areas with limited or no landline infrastructure. One key aspect that remains unclear until further research is done is exactly how Starlink's speeds compare to those offered by traditional providers. Understanding this will be crucial for making an informed decision about whether satellite internet is right for individual needs. Starlink's network is comprised of clusters of small satellites placed in low Earth orbit (LEO), providing a robust and redundant system for internet connectivity. With over 11,000 operational satellites as of October 2026, covering altitudes ranging from approximately 205 to 311 miles (330 to nearly 500 kilometers), the chances of a single satellite malfunction bringing down the entire network are slim. This redundancy is one of Starlink's most significant advantages over traditional internet connections. If one satellite in a cluster fails, another can take its place, minimizing downtime and ensuring continuous access. Even obstacles such as hills or buildings that might block signals from individual satellites are less likely to cause issues due to the presence of multiple satellites with viable angles. The sheer number of satellites in orbit is also set to increase, with SpaceX's recent application to operate up to 100,000 Gen3 satellites pending approval by the US Federal Communications Commission. This expansion will further enhance coverage and redundancy, making Starlink an increasingly reliable option for internet access. The cluster approach allows for more flexibility in positioning dishes, as there is often a satellite with a clear line of sight available even when obstacles are present. This can be particularly beneficial in areas where traditional internet connections are unreliable or unavailable. As the number of satellites in orbit continues to grow, so too does Starlink's potential for providing bulletproof internet access, assuming power outages and other rare disruptions are accounted for. With the right equipment and setup, users could enjoy virtually uninterrupted connectivity, making it an attractive option for those seeking a reliable internet solution. The Starlink satellite internet system boasts impressive resilience in theory, with its current-generation dishes capable of withstanding extreme temperatures and harsh weather conditions. These models can melt snow and endure temperatures ranging from -40 to 110 degrees Fahrenheit (-40 to 43 degrees Celsius), making them suitable for areas with varying climates. Additionally, when properly mounted, they are designed to withstand heavy rain and winds exceeding 99 miles per hour (about 160 kilometers per hour). However, in reality, Starlink's performance may not always live up to these expectations. Although the system can switch between satellites seamlessly, there can be brief disruptions while this process occurs, causing temporary connectivity issues. articles.title: Hard Disk Drives Show High Failure Rate Within First Year of Operation
articles.summary: A recent study by cloud storage giant Backblaze has found that nearly 1.5% of all HDDs fail within the first year of operation.
articles.content: A recent study by cloud storage giant Backblaze has shed light on a concerning issue with modern Hard Disk Drives (HDDs). The data reveals that nearly 1.5% of all HDDs fail within a year of operation, with the majority of these failures occurring in the first twelve months. According to Backblaze's analysis of over 350,000 storage drives, roughly 30% of failed HDDs break down without warning, leaving users unaware of any impending issues. This mechanical unpredictability is a significant problem for consumers and businesses alike, as it can lead to data loss and system downtime. The study also highlights the importance of manufacturing quality in determining an HDD's lifespan. Drives from certain manufacturers tend to be more reliable than others, with Seagate emerging as the most mechanically reliable across a recent analysis period. However, even within these brands, there are variations in reliability depending on specific models. Backblaze has been tracking its fleet of storage drives for several years and has developed a detailed understanding of their performance patterns. The company's data shows that HDDs typically last around 807 days before failing, although this figure only accounts for those drives that have already failed. Mechanical failures can be caused by a range of factors, including production defects, accidents such as power surges or drops, and damage to the drive's internal operating system. In some cases, these issues may be apparent through warning signs or error messages, but in many instances, they can occur without any prior indication. The cost-effectiveness of hard disk drives (HDDs) is a major factor contributing to their widespread adoption in data storage solutions. Despite being more prone to mechanical failures than solid-state drives (SSDs), HDDs remain significantly cheaper per gigabyte compared to other storage media. This disparity in pricing is particularly evident in the AI industry, where high-capacity storage is crucial for processing large datasets quickly. As demand for SSD storage continues to rise, driven by AI data centers, prices are increasing accordingly. However, for applications where cost is a top priority, HDDs offer an attractive option due to their lower per-unit costs. The data collected from over 5,000 drives reveals a clear correlation between the age of an HDD and its likelihood of failing. Specifically, the failure rate appears to increase significantly once a drive reaches seven years old. This trend suggests that users who rely on HDDs in their workflow should plan for regular replacements or invest in additional storage solutions. The relatively high failure rates of HDDs are not entirely unexpected, given the mechanical nature of these devices. As such, they can be seen as an inherent characteristic of this technology rather than a flaw. The limitations of current hard drive technology are becoming increasingly apparent as they continue to advance. The majority of drives rely on CMR (Conventional Magnetic Recording) tech, which provides reliable performance but is not without its drawbacks. As HDD manufacturers explore emerging technologies such as SMR and HAMR, it's clear that significant changes are needed to improve the resilience of these devices. Backblaze is keeping a close eye on these developments, although they have yet to incorporate them into their systems. Ultimately, data security requires a multi-layered approach that includes cloud, local, and off-site storage systems to safeguard against loss due to mechanical failure or other calamities. articles.title: Stock Market Selloff Highlights U.S. Debt Burden Fears
articles.summary: A brutal stock selloff last week has shed light on Wall Street's true fears about the growing U.S. debt burden, according to a top economist.
articles.content: A brutal stock selloff last week has shed light on Wall Street's true fears about the growing U.S. debt burden, according to a top economist. The 10-year Treasury yield had been rising sharply before easing in recent weeks as investors sought refuge in government bonds. However, its trajectory was marked by a significant spike of over 100 basis points, pushing it above 5% and reaching its highest level in 24 years at one point. This surge began after the outbreak of war with Iran in late February. The conflict sent oil prices soaring, prompting expectations that the Federal Reserve would raise interest rates to combat resurgent inflation. Meanwhile, hyperscalers have been flooding the bond market with fresh debt to finance massive capital expenditures and the AI infrastructure boom. This has sustained a hot economy and sticky inflation. This influx of debt from hyperscalers has competed for investors' dollars as the Treasury Department taps the bond market to finance its $2 trillion budget deficit and service the $40 trillion in U.S. debt. Some analysts have downplayed the spike in yields, attributing it to the crowding out effect caused by AI debt on the U.S. bond market. The recent market downturn has sparked a debate about the true drivers of rising bond yields in the US. According to Robin Brooks, a senior fellow at the Brookings Institution, the past week's selloff provides valuable insights into this issue. Brooks argues that the current market environment is not comparable to the IT bubble of the early 2000s, when corporate borrowing reached unprecedented levels. In contrast, public borrowing is now historically high and more likely driving up yields. The latest jobs report, which showed payrolls growing at a rate double what analysts had expected, also failed to support the argument that AI is responsible for higher yields. The bond market's reaction was particularly telling, with the two-year yield rising more than anticipated by hot economic growth. Brooks points out that the rise in yields following the jobs report cannot be explained solely by the prospect of strong economic growth. This suggests that investors are factoring in risks associated with the trajectory of US debt and deficits. The market-implied yield for a 10-year security 10 years from now is another indicator of these concerns, gauging the premium investors demand to hold Treasuries over the long term. The recent surge in long-term yields has been a major concern for investors and economists alike. One key indicator that suggests fiscal risk is at play is the 10-year10-year forward yield, which measures the market-implied yield for a 10-year security 10 years from now. This metric remained steady despite the decline in both 10-year and two-year yields, indicating that the increase in long-term yields is not solely driven by an AI bubble. In fact, this stability further supports the notion that fiscal risk is the primary driver of the market's concerns. The economist's observation highlights the significance of this indicator. The recent midterm elections and the subsequent sell-off in AI-related stocks have provided a unique opportunity to analyze the underlying factors contributing to rising long-term yields. By isolating these events, experts can better understand what is driving the market's behavior. According to the data, the increase in long-term yields is linked to growing fiscal stress. The federal budget deficit has been widening at an alarming rate, with the Treasury Department reporting a $1.99 trillion gap for fiscal year 2026, a 12% increase from the previous year. Revenue growth of 3% was outpaced by a 6% surge in spending, which is primarily driven by increasing interest payments on the national debt. The US government's growing national debt has led to a significant increase in interest payments, which have surpassed growth in total spending, revenue, and GDP. Net interest payments rose by 8% to $1.05 trillion, outpacing other areas of growth. This surge in interest costs is substantial, equating to approximately $2.9 billion per day. The Peter G. Peterson Foundation estimates that these net interest costs represent a staggering 3.2% of GDP, surpassing the previous record set in 1991. The alarming trend has prompted warnings from experts, who caution that the cycle of higher interest rates and debt could ultimately lead to a catastrophic outcome. Committee for a Responsible Federal Budget President Maya MacGuineas emphasized the urgency of addressing this issue, stating that "there are no easy fixes" and that it cannot be wished away. articles.summary: At least 34 people are confirmed dead after a migrant boat capsized off the coast of Senegal in the Atlantic Ocean.
articles.content: A migrant boat has capsized off the coast of Senegal in the Atlantic Ocean, resulting in a devastating loss of life. At least 34 people are confirmed dead, according to authorities who have been working to recover bodies from the disaster. The tragedy occurred along one of the most treacherous migration routes in the world, where thousands have perished over the years attempting to reach Spain's Canary Islands from West Africa. The route is notoriously hazardous, with many migrants facing perilous conditions at sea before they even arrive at their destination. Initial reports suggested that 21 bodies had been recovered and only one person was alive after being pulled from the water. However, as rescue efforts continued, the death toll rose to at least 34, according to a statement released by the Senegalese Press Agency (APS). The search for survivors is ongoing, with an "indeterminate number" of people still reported missing. The incident has highlighted the risks faced by migrants attempting to cross the Atlantic Ocean in search of a better life. The incident is being investigated by authorities in Senegal, who are working to locate those still missing and provide support to the families affected. According to Saliou Diouf, founder of Boza Fii, a migrant aid association based in Senegal, the sinking occurred on Friday, contradicting initial reports that it happened on Saturday. The nationalities of all the victims have not been confirmed due to ongoing search efforts. Senegal's President Bassirou Diomaye Faye has pledged to crack down on people organizing these perilous voyages, vowing to provide hope for young people in the country. He made this commitment through social media posts over the weekend. Thousands of West Africans attempt each year to reach Europe via the treacherous Atlantic route, a journey fraught with risks and uncertainties. Senegalese authorities have made a grim discovery off their coast, where a migrant boat has sunk in the Atlantic Ocean, resulting in at least 34 fatalities. The incident highlights the dangers faced by those attempting to reach Europe via this route. To add complexity to this issue, Senegalese police have intercepted another group of migrants on Friday who were trying to reach Spain on a similar small boat. This group consisted of 23 women, two babies, and two other children from various West African countries, including Senegal, Gambia, Guinea-Bissau, Guinea, and Nigeria. The Senegalese interior ministry has stated its determination to combat people smuggling networks by strengthening cooperation with neighboring countries. In a related development, the country's interior minister plans to visit the affected region to meet with families of the victims and express condolences on behalf of the state. In response to the surge in migrant boat arrivals, Spanish authorities on the Canary Island of El Hierro have declared an emergency, while Senegal, Mauritania, and Morocco have increased maritime patrols around departure points for small boats, forcing them to head further south towards the coasts of Gambia, Guinea-Bissau, and Guinea. Her win was by a narrow margin of just over 3,000 votes. Lacore credits her campaign's focus on building a broad coalition as key to her success. This move helped set the tone for reaching out to Independents and moderate Republicans who were crucial to winning the election. As a Democrat, Lacore's background is notable - she was previously registered as a Republican until 2016. Her decision to leave the party was motivated by her disagreement with Donald Trump's policies, but she declined to elaborate further on this aspect of her past. Lacore's campaign strategy was centered around appealing to voters beyond traditional Democratic Party lines. By securing endorsements from within the opposing party and targeting Independents and moderate Republicans, Lacore's team aimed to build a winning coalition that would carry her to victory in a district with a long history of Republican dominance. Lacore's team has been working on building a coalition that would carry her to victory in a district with a long history of bipartisan support. This strategy involves securing endorsements from within the opposing party and targeting Independents and moderate Republicans. The new Congress is expected to have a significant majority, which Lacore believes will provide opportunities for progress on key issues. With many veterans now elected to office, she notes that they tend to focus on achieving their mission rather than being bound by partisan politics. This non-partisan approach could potentially lead to more effective collaboration across party lines. Lacore's campaign promises included reducing the cost of housing, medical care, and healthcare, as well as eliminating tax breaks for data centers. She also plans to address rising costs driven by the ongoing war and tariffs imposed on various goods. The One Big Beautiful Bill has both positive and negative aspects, according to Rep.-elect Nancy Lacore. Lacore emphasized her support for tax breaks, specifically mentioning the exemption of tips and Social Security from taxes as a beneficial aspect of the bill. The imposition of tariffs through executive order has been a contentious issue in Congress, with Rep.-elect Lacore pointing out that they were not authorized by lawmakers. With corruption and cost of living being major concerns among voters, Rep.-elect Lacore stressed the need for unity across party lines on these issues. She noted that Americans are looking for accountability from their leaders, but also want them to address pressing problems without taking drastic measures. The public's desire for accountability is clear, but what does it mean in practice? Rep-elect Nancy Lacore suggests that accountability can take different forms depending on the specific issue at hand. One such area is stock trading by elected officials, a practice that has raised concerns about potential conflicts of interest. Lacore notes that putting rules in place to prevent this type of behavior would be an important step towards greater accountability. By doing so, she aims to restore public trust in government. As the highest-ranking female military officer ever elected to Congress, Lacore brings a unique perspective to Capitol Hill. She was relieved of her position as chief in August 2025 by Secretary Hegseth, who has since announced plans to cut the number of high-ranking officers by 20 percent and end diversity initiatives. articles.title: Dinner Served Early in the US
articles.summary: The timing of meals can have a significant impact on one's circadian rhythms and digestive system, with American dinnertime hours often differing from those of other countries.
articles.content: A common phenomenon for international visitors to the United States is the shock of being served dinner at what they consider an unreasonably early hour. This cultural discrepancy can be particularly disorienting for those who are accustomed to eating their main meal later in the evening. The disparity in dinnertime hours between the US and other countries is a notable characteristic of American culture. While visitors from abroad may struggle to adjust to this earlier schedule, it's not just a matter of personal preference - the timing of meals can have a significant impact on one's circadian rhythms and digestive system. One factor contributing to this peculiarity is the influence of traditional American customs and work patterns. The US has a unique blend of cultural values and lifestyle habits that shape when and how people eat their meals. This includes the widespread practice of eating dinner in the early evening, often between 5pm and 7pm. Social media platforms have also played a role in shaping American dinnertime trends, particularly among younger generations who are influenced by online content and social norms. As a result, earlier evening meals have become increasingly popular, further solidifying the US's reputation for eating dinner at an unusually early hour compared to other countries. The eating habits of Americans show a stark contrast when compared to those of other countries. In many parts of the world, dinner is served much later than the typical 5:00-6:00 pm in the US. This preference for earlier dinner times is reflected in American meal patterns. While breakfast and lunch are often light affairs, dinner takes center stage as the heartiest meal of the day. This is not surprising given that many people rely on a large evening meal to fuel their bodies after a long day. The practice of prioritizing dinner over other meals has significant implications for daily routines. Light breakfasts and lunches mean that Americans tend to feel hungrier earlier in the evening, making them ready to sit down to a big meal sooner rather than later. In contrast, many countries place greater emphasis on lunch as their main meal. This is particularly evident in Mexico, Spain, and numerous South American nations, where longer breaks are taken during the day to accommodate a filling midday meal. As a result, these cultures tend not to feel hungry until much later in the evening. The differences in eating habits between countries highlight the unique characteristics of American food culture. While other nations may enjoy a leisurely lunch and save their largest meal for dinner, Americans have developed a distinct preference that shows no signs of changing. The way people approach meals varies significantly across cultures, and one of the most striking differences is in the timing and size of lunch versus dinner. In many countries, including Mexico and those in South America, lunch is not only eaten earlier but also tends to be the largest meal of the day. This is partly due to the fact that these nations have longer breaks for lunch, allowing workers to take time off from their duties and enjoy a filling meal before returning to work. The American work schedule, which typically runs from 9 am to 5 pm with a brief break for lunch, contributes to the disparity in meal sizes. As a result, people often find themselves rushing through meals during this short window, leaving little room for a substantial dinner later on. Countries that take longer midday breaks are able to enjoy larger lunches without feeling pressured to get back to work immediately, giving them more time to relax and savor their food. The time zones in some countries can significantly impact daily schedules and meal times. In Spain, for example, the late sunset means that people often work during daylight hours, which pushes back their dinner time. This is not just a matter of convenience but also a practical necessity given the later evening hours. The influence of time zone on meal times is also evident in countries like the UK and Australia. These nations have a tradition of taking an afternoon snack called tea time, which serves as a midday break and allows people to delay their evening meal. This scheduling flexibility enables individuals to enjoy larger lunches without feeling rushed back into work. While Americans tend to eat around their work schedules, many other countries work around mealtimes. This approach acknowledges that meals are not just about sustenance but also an essential part of daily life, providing a break from work and allowing people to recharge. Meal times in different countries are often shaped by cultural and practical considerations beyond work schedules alone. Factors such as social norms, family obligations, and even local customs can influence when people choose to eat their main meals, resulting in varying patterns around the world. In many countries around the world, dinner is a leisurely affair that takes place late into the evening. For instance, in France, prime-time TV shows don't start until nearly 9 pm to accommodate the fact that people are still enjoying their meals at this hour. Similarly, Italians prioritize dining as an experience that allows for socializing and bonding with others over good food. This approach is reflected in the time they take to eat dinner, which can stretch into several hours. In contrast, Americans tend to view dinner more pragmatically, often treating it as just another item on their daily schedule. With a packed day of work, school, or other activities, many people are eager to fit in mealtime and get back to their busy lives. The influence of social media is also playing a role in shaping American attitudes towards dinnertime. Influencers are promoting early dinners as a key component of a healthy lifestyle, citing studies that suggest eating three hours before bedtime can improve digestion and sleep. Some Gen Z influencers have even adopted the mantra "dinner by 8, in bed by 9" as a way to prioritize their well-being and maintain a balance between work, rest, and play. The traditional American dinner hour has long been a topic of interest, often drawing comparisons to eating habits in other parts of the world. While some cultures enjoy a late evening meal, Americans tend to prioritize an early dinner, typically between 5pm and 7pm. This preference for earlier meals is largely influenced by societal expectations and work schedules, which can make it challenging to eat later in the day. As a result, many people have adopted routines that accommodate this earlier dinner time, such as winding down with a relaxing evening routine after finishing their meal. This has become an integral part of American culture, reflecting the country's unique lifestyle and values. articles.title: Godzilla Minus Zero Breaks North American Box Office Records
articles.summary: The Japanese film "Godzilla Minus Zero" opened with $31.6 million in North America, surpassing previous records.
articles.content: A Japanese film has broken records at the North American box office with a massive opening weekend haul of $31.6 million. The film, "Godzilla Minus Zero, is a sequel to 2023's Oscar-winning movie Godzilla Minus One and marks a return to the series' Japanese roots. The success of Godzilla Minus Zero comes at the expense of Warner Bros.' animated The Cat in the Hat movie, which opened with $20.5 million over the weekend, along with an additional $10 million from international markets. The film features voice acting by Bill Hader. The revival of the Godzilla franchise is a significant achievement for director Takashi Yamazaki, who has managed to breathe new life into one of the longest-running movie franchises. The film's success also highlights the growing demand for foreign-language content in North America. Despite this impressive opening, Godzilla Minus Zero still trails behind another notable foreign-language film, 2004's Passion of the Christ, which opened with $83.8 million despite featuring largely Aramaic dialogue. The record-breaking opening of Godzilla Minus Zero has set a new benchmark for live-action films worldwide. With a debut weekend total of $31.6 million in North America, it surpasses the previous mark held by 2004's Hero, which launched with $17.9 million. This milestone is part of a growing trend where international, non-English productions are captivating American audiences at cinemas. The success of Godzilla Minus Zero follows closely on the heels of other foreign-language films that have achieved impressive box office numbers in North America. The Indian epic Ramayana: Rise of a Legend also made its mark over the weekend, achieving the widest North American release for an Indian film to date. With a domestic launch of $8.7 million and a total of $32 million earned in India, this Hindi-language production is the most expensive Indian film ever made. In Japan, Godzilla Minus Zero raked in approximately $17 million over the weekend, while Ramayana: Rise of a Legend was given a global release alongside its American debut. The simultaneous global rollout was built on the idea that audiences worldwide connect with Godzilla and the vision of director Takashi Yamazaki, according to Koji Ueda, president of Toho Global. The film's unexpected success is a testament to its wide appeal and strong marketing strategy. With a modest budget of less than $20 million, Godzilla Minus Zero has already exceeded expectations by raking in millions at the box office. Its performance on large-format screens has been particularly impressive, with 34% of its global take coming from IMAX showings that generated $21.3 million worldwide. This suggests that the film's visual spectacle is a major draw for audiences. The success of Godzilla Minus Zero may also have implications for future Godzilla films, including the upcoming Hollywood production Godzilla x Kong: Supernova. If this latest installment continues to perform well at the box office, it will be interesting to see how it compares to its predecessor in terms of audience reception and critical acclaim. Meanwhile, other animated films are struggling to find their footing. The new animated take on The Cat in the Hat has failed to generate significant interest among moviegoers, despite receiving a relatively modest budget of $86 million. Laika's stop motion animated fantasy Wildwood is an exception, having performed well at the box office and even briefly leading all films early in the week. Its success may indicate that audiences are still eager for high-quality animated storytelling. The box office results for last weekend's new releases were mixed, with Wildwood experiencing a 22% dip in its third weekend to $7 million. Despite this drop, the film has still managed to accumulate a respectable domestic total of $39.8 million. In third place was Angel Studios' musical drama Drummer Boy, which opened with a strong $9.3 million on its debut weekend. The film's soundtrack also reached number one on the iTunes chart, suggesting that audiences are responding well to the movie's music. Another notable success story from last weekend was Martin McDonagh's dark comedy Wild Horse Nine. With an opening weekend total of $6 million domestic and $6.6 million internationally, the film has exceeded expectations for a prestige awards contender. This performance is particularly impressive given that the film launched in only 1,100 domestic theaters. The success of Wild Horse Nine is expected to boost its chances of receiving Oscar nominations, following its well-received premiere at the Venice Film Festival. The Searchlight Pictures release will expand its theater count significantly next weekend, with a projected doubling of its current number of screens. In limited releases, two potential Oscar contenders got off to promising starts. Jordan Firstman's Club Kid debuted with a strong $65,097 average from six screens for A24, while Peter Farrelly's I Play Rocky" launched with a $49,200 per-screen average from seven theaters for Amazon MGM Studios. The documentary "You Can See Everything" directed by Nathan Fiedler and Lance Oppenheim has continued its impressive run at the box office. In its fourth weekend of release, it earned a significant $8.9 million in ticket sales. This success adds to the film's overall North American earnings, which now stand at $79.8 million. The documentary, which delves into the life of Elizabeth Holmes, has clearly resonated with audiences. The box office saw a substantial increase over the previous weekend, with overall ticket sales rising by 96.8%.
